comment.narrative: The crisis in Lebanon is often referred to as multifaceted as it can be felt on various levels including the political the financial social and even societal. Through the first work package which has convened a group of experts and opinionleaders GEOL coming from diverse geographical religious and political backgrounds to agree on potential reform and policy options as well as a future vision for the country including the values that unite the Lebanese populace. Thus this work package addresses major debates on political reform as well as social and societal norms that could potentially govern a future Lebanon. With that one cannot talk of the future of the country without reverting to its violent past especially in the absence of reconciliation and transitional justice. For that reason the political societal and social crises are often compounded by a lack of closure on the wounds of the past that seem to yield continuousand at times violentclashes. Finally as the state lacks the wherewithal to deliver services as it spirals into complete collapse the project also serves to respond to the evergrowing need when it comes to service provision. More than that as we are implementing in localities across Lebanon who not only have very limited access to services but also suffer from a violent crossconfessional history we also aim to strengthen social cohesion in those areas as well as contribute to grassroots reconciliation.

To add it seems that little to no communication channels exist between political parties which has only served to increase polarization amid the current political paraylsis and deadlock

This is especially true in work packages 2 and 3 wherein the key project stakeholders are engaged in the implementation of the projects and retain ownership over the process. It is also important to note that as Berghof ensures that all key political and community leaders are engaged this has afforded the project team a greater sense of credibility through implementation.
